//: How level 1 is generated. Run it with: powershell -File tools/rebuild_level.ps1 -Level level_1
notes: This is the only level whose .tscn is both input and output of a tool chain:
gen_farm_playground.gd loads the committed scene, mutates it and saves back over it.
MEASURED 2026-09-02 by replaying this chain twice from the committed state:
- The PAINT half is a fixed point. Both splat PNGs came back byte-identical on the
second pass. The first pass was not identical because the COMMITTED paint was stale:
it gained 2073 px of asphalt (0 lost), a ~1 px rim along the whole ring road. City
roads are lane_width 4.8 (kit/roads/city_profile.tres, over a 3.5 default), and the
asphalt paint had never been re-run after that widening -- so ~2000 m2 of paved road
edge was carrying grass/dirt grip instead of asphalt. That is the drift this manifest
exists to catch, and it was invisible until the chain became runnable.
- The SCULPT half does NOT converge exactly. Each replay moves ~150-250 heightmap px
by 1-3 of the 8-bit height steps (0.2-0.6 m), always in the farm's blend rims, never
in a flat. _flatten re-lerps its rim on already-flat ground and _smooth runs 4 passes
over an already-smoothed rim; neither is idempotent, and the tool header says so.
It is not material: the farm's own acceptance report is byte-identical across replays
(ramp grades 8.1 / 13.7 / 24.2 deg, wallow floor 26.00..26.60, worst exit facet
0.20 m, 0 backward steps). A replay is safe; it is just not bit-reproducible.
That is why the heightmap carries a "sculpt_drift" tolerance below instead of being
held to byte equality: the replay driver decodes the two copies and judges the pixel
count and step delta, so a real change still reads as drift while the rim churn does
not. Widen the tolerance only with a reason; do not delete it to silence a report.
ORDER: the farm runs before the asphalt paint. Measured, the two are spatially disjoint
today -- 0 of the 12045 asphalt px fall inside any farm rect -- so the order changes
nothing right now. It is recorded this way because it is the order that stays correct if
the farm ever grows toward a road: the farm's first act is to repaint GRASS over every
rect it flattened, which would erase asphalt underneath it, while asphalt painted last
simply wins on the road. Do not flip it.
The --import steps are not decoration. gen_farm_playground's `build` stage leaves every
scatter canvas's stored_ground_hash EMPTY so that a skipped `resnap` fails the bake
loudly, and `resnap` cannot compute the real hash until the sculpted heightmap has been
back through the importer.
If you press Auto-splat on this terrain it reclassifies channels 0..3 from the heightmap
and ZEROES splatmap2 -- which is correct (a surviving 4..7 weight would double-count
against the fresh base), and which destroys Field, Mud, Gravel and the road asphalt.
Recovering means replaying this chain, not undoing the button.
//sculpt_drift: Per-source PNG allowance for a sculpt whose ops cannot be idempotent. A file with no entry is held to byte equality. Measured over repeated replays: 150-250 px, 1-3 of the 8-bit steps, always in the farm's blend rims.

steps.what: Terrain Generate (island preset) + hand brush sculpt + Auto-splat + hand paint, then RoadPath Draw + Conform, prop dressing and scatter painting -- all in the editor.
steps.why: Hand work. It lives in the committed heightmap/splat PNGs and in the .tscn's road curves, prop transforms and stored scatter transforms; no tool reproduces it. This is what a replay starts FROM, not something a replay runs.

Sculpts the field / paddock / yard / wallow / haul ramp into the heightmap, paints Field, Mud and Gravel, rebuilds the farm nodes and the tractor spawn, and saves the .tscn. Leaves stored_ground_hash empty on purpose.
ScatterBase.ground_hash reads the heightmap TEXTURE, so resnap cannot run until the sculpted PNG is back through the importer.
Re-snaps scatter Ys onto the new ground and stamps the real ground hash. A clean replay prints '0 instances moved' -- that is the PNG round-tripping byte-exactly.

Stamps channel 6 (Asphalt) under every RoadPath corridor at the profile's paved_half_width, so grip_at reads road on-road and terrain off-road. Writes the splat PNGs only -- it never saves the .tscn. Re-run it after ANY road or road-profile edit; nothing else notices that the paint went stale.
